# Egress list

By default no data leaves a self-hosted installation except calls the customer configures (`SEC-163`). This page lists every kind of outbound connection the Plux Server can make. It is generated from the registry of destinations in `backend/internal/httpx/destinations.go`, and a test fails when it differs: a new outbound call cannot ship without an entry here.

Every outbound connection is built for one of these kinds. A kind with fixed hosts refuses any other host when it connects. A kind without fixed hosts goes to an address the customer enters, and the SSRF policy refuses private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses unless the installation allows them (`SEC-104`, `SEC-105`).

| Destination | Purpose | Configured by | Hosts | Default | Data sent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Android attestation status list (`attestation.android-status-list`) | Revocation check of Android key attestation certificates (SEC-002). | operator: attestation.android.statusListFile (a local file replaces the download) | `android.googleapis.com` | on | A plain GET of Google's public list; nothing about devices or apps. |
| Apple App Attest receipts (`attestation.apple-receipt`) | Refreshes the App Attest receipt to read the fraud metric. | operator: attestation.apple.fraudReceipt.enabled | `data.appattest.apple.com`, `data-development.appattest.apple.com` | off | The receipt of a device and a request token signed with the team's key. |
| Push services (`push`) | Silent push that tells a device to sync (SYN-060). | operator: push.enabled, plus per-app credentials | `api.push.apple.com`, `api.sandbox.push.apple.com`, `fcm.googleapis.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com` | off | A push token and a content-free wake-up payload; the credential exchange sends a signed assertion. |
| Notification channels and webhooks (`notify.http`) | Slack, Teams, Telegram and outbound webhook messages about events in an organisation. | organisation: Notification channels (Studio, Settings) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | The event text; Telegram goes to api.telegram.org, the others to the address entered. |
| Mail relay (`notify.smtp`) | Email notifications. | organisation: Notification channels (Studio, Settings) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | The event text and the recipients. |
| Analytics OTLP export (`analytics.otlp`) | Sends daily aggregates of an organisation's analytics to its own collector. | organisation: Analytics export (Studio, Analytics) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | Rollups only: counts and sums, never an event or a device identifier. |
| Analytics webhook export (`analytics.webhook`) | Posts an organisation's analytics events to its own receiver as signed Standard Webhooks messages (enterprise edition, ANL-011). | organisation: Analytics export files and webhook (Studio, Analytics) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | Batches of the organisation's raw events with their device class and locale; never a device secret or a user identifier. |
| Audit export (`audit.export`) | Streams the audit log to a SIEM as syslog, CEF, OTLP logs or a signed webhook. | organisation: Audit export destinations (Studio, Settings) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | Audit entries of the organisation; secrets are never part of an entry. |
| Gateway upstreams (`gateway.upstream`) | The services an app's devices reach through the secure gateway (SEC-030). | organisation: Gateway upstreams (Studio, Gateway) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | The device's request, with the credentials the upstream's configuration names. |
| Identity provider key sets (`gateway.identity`) | Verifies the identity tokens a device exchanges at the gateway. | organisation: Gateway identity providers (Studio, Gateway) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | A GET of the provider's discovery document and key set. |
| OpenID Connect sign-in (`auth.oidc`) | Single sign-on for people (SEC-100). | operator: auth.studio.oidc.issuer | the address the customer enters | none until configured | The authorisation code exchange and the provider's key set. |
| CI provider keys (`auth.ci-issuer`) | Verifies the identity tokens of CI pipelines (SRV-064). | operator: auth.ci.issuers | the address the customer enters | none until configured | A GET of the provider's discovery document and key set. |
| Git remotes (`gitsync.remote`) | Exports an app to a Git repository on publish (GOV-011). | organisation: Git export (Studio, App settings) | the address the customer enters | none until configured | The app's documents in the SCH-006 layout, with the stored credential. |
| Server traces (`observability.otlp`) | Exports the server's own traces to the operator's collector (OBS-001). | operator: observability.otlpEndpoint | the address the customer enters | off | Spans of the server's requests; no payloads, no secrets. |
| Function egress proxy (`functions.egress`) | The upstream calls of a Plux Function, through the CONNECT proxy of the function runner (FN-013). | organisation: The domains a function declares and an administrator approves | the address the customer enters | off | Whatever the function sends to a domain it is allowed. |

## Not egress

The installation also connects to services its operator runs and names. Nothing reaches a third party through them:

- PostgreSQL (`database.url`)
- The cache, Valkey or Redis (`cache.valkeyURL`)
- The object store (`objectStorage.*`)
- HashiCorp Vault or a PKCS#11 module for the signing keys (`signing.vault`, `signing.pkcs11`)
- The document scanner (`assets.malwareScanner`)
- Mutual-TLS calls between the roles of one installation (`internalTLS.*`)
